verdicts.reason: Every quote verified verbatim and the contradiction is normative, not stylistic. BLOCKED side: 14.01.01-digital-product-listing-spec-sheet.md:127 ('Vendor tries to buy their own listing | Blocked. Self-purchase is a free path to manufactured sales rank...') and :213 D-09 ('Self-purchase is blocked on the same surface'), plus 14.01.01:76 ('Is the vendor | No buy control'); 14.08.01-vendor-onboarding-product-submission.md:134 ('Blocked - self-purchase games sales rank... No buy control'). PERMITTED side: 14.02.01-licence-issuance-entitlement-record.md:201 D-11 ('Self-purchase is permitted and flagged'), :158 DT-10 ('cannot be blocked'), :105, :27; 14.04.01-sample-loop-pack-catalog.md:174 ('Not blocked - blocking it teaches vendors to use a second account, which is worse'); 14.07.01-perpetual-purchase-ownership.md:140 ('Permitted and flagged'). Two further permitted-side statements the finding did not cite strengthen it: 14.03.03-licence-portal-purchased-library.md:192 ('Buying your own product is normal... and is not a signal by itself') and 14.09.02-digital-refund-eligibility-adjudication.md:169, which routes self-purchase refunds to fraud review and therefore presupposes the purchase exists. Neither side carries a [PENDING]/[OWNER] marker; each cites the other file as authority (14.08.01:134 cites 14.01.01 D-09; 14.02.01 D-11 is cited by 14.04.01/14.07.01). No index, CX or moscow-ledger entry reconciles them - searched the whole domain for a reconciling row and found none. 14.08.01's substitute (14.02.05 D-16, verified at 14.02.05-licence-terms-registry.md:205) covers only 'a vendor places their own product into a project', not a purchase, so the blocked reading genuinely leaves the purchase path with no defined entitlement. Two competent implementers diverge on UI (buy control present/absent), data (flagged entitlement vs none) and downstream filters. Blocking upheld.

Counts verified exactly: `grep -rn 'PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5'` returns 23 hits across 19 files, matching the claim. The target stage is demonstrably complete: digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:133-134 close Q-01/Q-02 with 'RESOLVED ... | Agent | (done) /ideate-discover'; 14.01.01-digital-product-listing-spec-sheet.md:222 closes Q-02 with '(done) /ideate-discover Step 5'; 14.01.03-host-dependency-graph.md:96 reads 'RESOLVED (D-03, Step 5)'. The successor stage is also complete - 14.01.01:220, :224, 14.01.03:95, :97, digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:135-139 and 14.06.03:96-97 all say 'Deferral re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-validate`' (or 're-targeted: `/ideate-validate` has already run'), and /ideate-validate runs after /ideate-discover. So the authors' own convention treats a completed stage as a dead target and they applied the re-pointing to Open Questions rows only, never to these in-body markers. This is exactly the rule-2 carve-out: the deferral is tracked in form but malformed in substance - the marker names no owner and points at a stage that cannot run again in sequence. Not a contradiction and not a missing decision, so warning rather than blocking is correct. Note the individual behaviour-bearing instances the finding chains to (#003 and #005-#008) are separately refuted below on their merits; the tracking defect stands on its own.

But the feature is explicitly cut: moscow-ledger.md:750 places 14.02.03 in the WONT band (WONT section begins at moscow-ledger.md:713) with the rationale 'a DRM bridge is a business-development negotiation wearing an integration's costume - PACE has no self-serve reseller API ... only needed for third-party commercial plugins the store cannot obtain at launch'. Two further gates sit above it: 14.02.03 Q-01 ('Is authorised-reseller status ... obtainable at all ... a BD question that gates the feature') routed to /create-prd-stack, and Q-03 ('Should offline activation exist at all') routed to /create-prd, both with owners. digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:135 Q-03 records the same banding ('14.02.03 `WONT`'). No implementer is forced to invent compensating behaviour for a feature the ledger says will not be built and whose existence is an owner question with a live target. The forced-invention premise therefore fails even though the two rows are genuinely undecided.

verdicts.reason: All four quotes verified verbatim, but the advisory-vs-enforced 'self-contradiction' is the finding's own reading, not the text's. D-03 at 14.05.04-tagged-preview-untagged-delivery.md:95 says the platform 'recommends a minimum tag density rather than accepting any interval' - the contrast drawn is recommend-vs-silently-accept-anything, and the word 'refuse' or 'block' appears nowhere in it. Every other mention agrees it is advisory: the Happy Path at :41 leaves the interval to 'the producer's chosen interval'; the too-sparse edge case at :51 says 'Producer's choice; the platform should recommend a minimum density, not just accept any value'; the symmetric too-dense row at :52 likewise says 'Producer's choice'. The States gate at :68 is presence-only and matches D-01 at :93 ('A beat cannot publish publicly without a tag') exactly - no density gate is implied or contradicted. Two competent implementers both build: mandatory tag, advisory density hint, producer decides. The residual - no numeric default for the recommendation - is a tunable copy/threshold constant on an advisory hint, not product behaviour that must be invented, and Q-01/Q-03 at :100/:102 keep the surrounding tagging-sufficiency question owned and targeted at /create-prd.
verdicts.evidence: 14.05.04-tagged-preview-untagged-delivery.md:95 (D-03), :41, :51, :52 (both edge rows say 'Producer's choice'), :68 and :93 (presence gate matches D-01), :100 and :102 (Q-01/Q-03 owned, targeted /create-prd)

verdicts.reason: Quote verified at 14.04.03-project-template-catalog-dependency-manifest.md:55 and the three questions at :100-102 are as described. The behaviour is nevertheless governed by 14.01.03, which the domain routes this exact case to. 14.01.03-host-dependency-graph.md:53 rules the delisted-dependency case in full: 'Vendor of the dependency exits the platform (14.08.05) | The joinable edge degrades to external: existing owners keep the dependency and their edges stay satisfied, but the inline add-to-cart is withdrawn... A buyer who does not already own it can no longer satisfy the edge on WeJammin. | New buyer... edge renders unsatisfied with the remedy demoted to advisory - "Requires X (no longer sold here) - you must obtain it elsewhere." Pre-purchase, not post-download.' 14.01.03:84 states the routing explicitly: 'a template's manifest is a many-edge instance of this same graph'. The sibling feature resolves the identical scenario the same way and cites that file - 14.04.02-preset-patch-catalog.md:60 ('the bank is still fine for existing owners but uncompletable for new buyers | 14.01.03 edge case'), with the pre-checkout race handled at 14.04.02:58 ('Purchase is blocked at the gate'). The 14.04 CX frames the same case as affecting new buyers, not post-purchase holders: 14.04-sound-content-catalogs-cx.md:78 ('leaves a template permanently uncompletable for new buyers'). Post-purchase loss of third-party function is separately settled by 14.04.02:57 P-12/D-04: 'an external compatibility change... No default refund and no vendor obligation attach to a third-party change.' Refund/notify/substitute is therefore answered, not invented.

Quotes verified at 14.05.02-exclusive-rights-purchase-auto-delist.md:51, :90 (D-03) and digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:359 (CX-18 q5). But the substantive outcome of the lease-wins-the-race ordering is fully determined, not open. digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:347 (CX-18 relationship) states the rule for both orderings: exclusive issuance 'must NOT revoke prior non-exclusive leases - grandfathering is the market norm', and :356 q2 'prior non-exclusive leases explicitly preserved'. A lease that commits before the exclusive is by definition prior, so it is grandfathered; 14.05.02 Q-01 at :96 confirms it as RESOLVED ('they survive; the buyer takes subject to them', on 09.01.03 D-03 'Encumbrances attach to the asset and travel'). CX-18 q5 supplies the complementary ordering. Together they leave no undefined lease or entitlement outcome. What remains is only whether the D-03 lease count is re-rendered at commit - a disclosure-freshness mechanism, and domain 14 already owns a general rule for display-vs-commit divergence at the cart: 14.01.01-digital-product-listing-spec-sheet.md:208 D-04 ('bind what was displayed, not what is current at commit', following domain CX-04 q5) with the consent-break family at digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:270-273, tracked as a cart-rail obligation in 14.01.01:223 Q-04 (→ /create-prd-architecture) and digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:546. That residue is downstream mechanism, not undefined product behaviour. 14.05.02 is also COULD-banded (moscow-ledger.md:609, COULD section from :507).

Quotes verified at 14.02.04-serial-blacklisting-anti-piracy.md:52, :87 (D-01) and :95-97. The central claim - 'whether an automatic chargeback-driven blacklist exists at all is itself unstated' - is contradicted by the same file. 14.02.04:38 (Happy Path 1) makes the chargeback a detection input, not an action: 'Abuse is detected or reported (vendor report, leaked-serial monitoring, chargeback signal)', and D-01 at :87 plus D-02 at :88 then force adjudication with 'a reason, a notification, and an appeal route' before any state change. There is no automatic path, so the card-theft victim is protected by exactly the due-process the file already mandates. The entitlement-side consequence of a chargeback is separately and precisely specified: 14.02.01-licence-issuance-entitlement-record.md:200 D-10 (chargeback a distinct trigger everywhere), :83, :127 and :138 (chargeback → revoked); 14.03.03-licence-portal-purchased-library.md:175 ('Row → `revoked`, reason "payment reversed". The appeal route is the payment dispute, not our appeals process'); 14.07.01-perpetual-purchase-ownership.md:128; and digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:365/:375 (CX-19). Who bears the chargeback loss is itself a tracked owner question at 14.02.01:210 Q-03 (→ /create-prd). The blacklist half is additionally gated by 14.02.04:95 Q-01 ([OWNER] → /create-prd). Nothing here forces invention.

The row is verified at 14.06.03-bundled-software-with-used-hardware.md:52, but the finding materially misstates the tracking: it says 'the two tracked questions do not reach the unwind' when the file carries three, and Q-03 at 14.06.03:99 is the unwind, verbatim - 'If the hardware is returned after the licence transferred and the buyer has activated it on a machine that never comes back online, who eats the loss? | User | /create-prd'. That is precisely the finding's own stated forced invention ('who absorbs the loss'), owned and targeted. Q-01 at :97 owns the prior half ('when does the licence leg settle - payment, delivery, or inspection-window close? ... the owner must name the loser', → /create-prd). Whether a hardware return reverses the transfer at all is also settled outside the file: 14.09.03-licence-revocation-entitlement-clawback.md:11 and :33 enumerate hardware return as a first-class revocation trigger ('or hardware is returned with its bundled software (14.06.03), the entitlement must' claw back), :40 lists it in the trigger set, and :87 records the touchpoint; digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:365 confirms '14.09.03 currently enumerates refund / transfer / hardware-return'. The reconciliation with 14.09.02 D-12 is not in tension either - D-12 governs refundability of a transferred-out entitlement, while the hardware return is a clawback trigger, a distinction 14.09.03:33 draws explicitly. The scenario is further below the launch set (moscow-ledger.md:612 places 14.06.03 in COULD; digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:142 Q-08 records 'the transfer market is cut', with 14.06.02 in WONT).
